value.name: Asha leaves the house with Marcus
value.description: Asha hears voices inside, does not stop to listen, and steps out of the house with Marcus.
evidence: Asha could hear the low murmur of voices — Lucia's, mostly, and occasionally Rosa's, and once Daniel's, not arguing, just speaking. She did not stop to listen. She let Marcus open the front door and she stepped out onto the stoop

value.name: Cold air shocks Asha outside
value.description: The February air hits Asha as she stands blinking on the top step.
evidence: the February air took her like a slap and she stood there for a second on the top step blinking at the brightness of it

value.name: Marcus offers to drive
value.description: Marcus asks if he should drive, and Asha agrees.
evidence: "You want me to drive," Marcus said.

value.name: Marcus drives Asha to the office
value.description: Marcus drives east on Spruce toward the office without turning on the radio.
evidence: In the car, heading east on Spruce toward the office, Marcus did not turn on the radio, which was his small mercy.

value.name: Asha reflects on the letter and Daniel's invitation
value.description: Asha thinks about the letter in the banker’s box, Rosa's gesture, Daniel's lunch invitation, and her need to be careful about mistaking relief for permission.
evidence: Asha put her head back against the seat and closed her eyes and let the city slide past her in the dark behind her eyelids.
She thought about the letter in the banker's box on the back seat.
She thought about Rosa's hand pressing flat against the table.

She thought about Daniel asking her to stay for lunch and about the particular tone in which he had asked, which had been the tone of a man asking for something he had not known he was allowed to want, and she thought about how careful she was going to have to be, in the weeks ahead, not to mistake the relief of being asked for the permission to say yes.

value.name: Asha asks Marcus to warn her
value.description: Asha asks Marcus to tell her if she starts spending too much time at that house.
evidence: "If I start spending too much time at that house, tell me."

value.name: Marcus promises repeated warning
value.description: Marcus promises to tell Asha and to keep warning her even if she ignores him at first.
evidence: "I promise you," Marcus said, "that I will tell you, and I also promise you that you will not listen the first time, and I promise you that I will tell you again."

value.name: Asha laughs at Marcus's warning
value.description: Asha gives a brief, nearly silent laugh in response to Marcus's promise.
evidence: She laughed once, short, almost soundless.
